description: An enumerator piped through xargs into a remove verb is the whole-tree wipe with its operands arriving on stdin, and until 2026-09-16 no tier saw it on either tool (DEF-826): the find arm needs a delete action and this find carries none, the remove verb behind the carrier has no operand for the zone check or the rm tiers to read, and the speed bump had nothing to bump. Driven on fresh throwaways under /bin/bash and pwsh 7.6.5: every spelling left the root standing and empty; the narrowed one took only its matches. Now the enumerator's roots are the remove verb's operands on both tools, judged through the same three tiers as the direct pipe on the PowerShell tool (DEF-822): the wall from a catastrophic root, the roster pass, one nudge. DEF-831 (2026-09-16): the version-control listing joins the heads on both tools with a roots reader of its own -- the tracked-files listing piped through the carrier, or straight into the cmdlet, reached on both tools and drew no tier (driven on a throwaway repository: the tracked files went, the untracked one stayed).
fix_commit: the carrier lane, 2026-09-16 (DEF-826); the listing head, 2026-09-16 (DEF-831)
fix_module: tools/cc/hooks/_bash_patterns.py::has_catastrophic_piped_remove + has_catastrophic_bash_sweep + _bash_pipeline_roots + _git_listing_roots + _enum_head_key + _PIPED_REMOVE_RE + iter_unnarrowed_bash_sweep_roots; tools/cc/hooks/write_guard.py (CATASTROPHIC_PIPED_REMOVE); tools/cc/hooks/_speedbump.py (the Bash branch reads the union); the PowerShell twin through _PS_PIPED_REMOVE_RE's head position and carrier segment
